faqs.q: Which English test do I need?
faqs.a: It depends on the university. Most accept IELTS, TOEFL or PTE.

faqs.q: How much money do I need to show for a visa?
faqs.a: Usually the first year's tuition plus living costs. We will give you the exact figure for your country.

faqs.q: Can I apply with a low GPA?
faqs.a: Yes, many universities look at the whole profile. We can suggest options that suit your results.

blog.title: How to write a strong statement of purpose
blog.excerpt: A clear structure that admissions officers like to read.
blog.author: Sita Sharma
blog.body: Start with a specific moment that led you to your subject. Explain what you have done since, why this course fits, and what you will do after graduating. Keep it to one page and avoid repeating your CV.

blog.title: Budgeting for your first year abroad
blog.excerpt: Tuition is only part of the cost.
blog.author: Bikash Poudel
blog.body: Add tuition, rent, food, transport, health cover and a small emergency fund. Check each university’s cost-of-living estimate and compare it to your funds proof.

blog.title: IELTS or PTE: which should you take?
blog.excerpt: Both are widely accepted. Here is how to choose.
blog.author: Sita Sharma
blog.body: IELTS has a human speaking examiner, while PTE is fully computer-scored with faster results. Check your target university’s accepted tests first, then pick the format that suits you.

blog.title: Scholarships you can apply for this year
blog.excerpt: Where to look and when to apply.
blog.author: Bikash Poudel
blog.body: Start with the scholarship pages of your chosen universities, then check government programs such as Chevening and DAAD. Deadlines are often months before the application deadline, so plan early.

blog.title: Your visa interview: what to expect
blog.excerpt: Common questions and how to prepare.
blog.author: Sita Sharma
blog.body: Officers want to confirm that you are a genuine student with a clear plan and enough funds. Know your course, your university and your finances, and answer briefly and honestly.
